`StandardJSONSupplier.ensure_ascii` decides whether non-ASCII characters in serialized JSON are written as `\uXXXX` escapes or as literal characters. It is a thin wrapper over the `ensure_ascii` argument of Python's `json.dumps`.

**Where it is defined**
- The attribute is `StandardJSONSupplier.ensure_ascii = True` at `src/quill/json/supplier.py:144`. `StandardJSONSupplier` is the default `app.json` supplier and is built on the stdlib `json` module.
- Its docstring says it replaces non-ASCII characters with escape sequences. This can be more compatible with some clients. Setting it to `False` gives better performance and smaller output.
- The abstract base `JSONSupplier` has no such setting. Only the stdlib-based subclass does.

**How it takes effect**
- `StandardJSONSupplier.dumps` (`supplier.py:166-179`) calls `kwargs.assumefallback("ensure_ascii", self.ensure_ascii)` and then `json.dumps(obj, **kwargs)`.
- The attribute is only a default. A caller can pass `ensure_ascii=...` directly to `app.json.dumps` and override it for that call.
- `StandardJSONSupplier.response` (`supplier.py:189-215`) builds its body through `self.dumps(obj, **dump_args)`. `dump_args` only sets `indent` or `separators`. Responses built by `quill.notationize` and `app.json.response` therefore follow the attribute too.

**Effect on the output**
- With `True`, the default, a non-ASCII character such as `é` comes out as `"\u00e9"`. Characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane come out as surrogate-pair escapes. The output is pure ASCII.
- With `False`, the characters are written literally, for example `"é"`. The response is then encoded as UTF-8 by the response class.
- Either way the decoded data is identical. Only the wire representation changes.
- `loads` (`supplier.py:181-187`) is unaffected. It parses both forms.

**Configuration**
- The old `JSON_AS_ASCII` config key was deprecated in 2.2.0 and removed in 2.3.0 (`CHANGES.rst`).
- To change the behavior, set the attribute on the supplier, for example `app.json.ensure_ascii = False`. Alternatively, subclass `StandardJSONSupplier` or assign a different supplier.

**Bug in this checkout**
The card for this file notes that `dumps` and `response` call `assumefallback` on plain dicts, which don't have that method. The stdlib equivalent is `setdefault`. This came from the compiled index and I didn't run the code to check it. If it holds, `ensure_ascii` would never be applied, because `dumps` would fail first.

`Schematic._got_registered_once` is a class-level flag that records whether a schematic has been enrolled on an app at least once. Its job is to stop setup methods from changing the schematic after that point. Otherwise later changes would apply inconsistently across apps.

**Where it lives (`src/quill/sansio/schematics.py`)**
- `Schematic._got_registered_once = False` is defined at line 172. Instances inherit `False` until enrollment sets it on the instance.
- `Schematic.enroll(app, options)` sets `self._got_registered_once = True` at line 320. That happens right after `app.schematics[name] = self`, and before `build_registration_state` and the run of `deferred_functions`.
- `Schematic._verify_configuration_completed(f_name)` at lines 213-221 is the check. If the flag is set, it raises an `AssertionError`. The message says the setup method `f_name` can no longer be called on the schematic `self.name`. It explains that the schematic was already registered at least once, so any changes won't be applied consistently. It tells the user to finish all imports, decorators and functions before registering.

**How the check is triggered (`src/quill/sansio/skeleton.py`)**
- The `preparationmethod` decorator (lines 42-49) wraps a method so that `self._verify_configuration_completed(f.__name__)` runs before the method body.
- `Armature` (lines 52-698) is the shared base class of `Schematic` and `App`. Its setup methods carry this decorator: `route`, the verb shortcuts, `attach_link_regulation`, `terminus`, `preceding_inquiry`, `following_inquiry`, `dismantle_query`, `scope_enricher`, `link_argument_prepare_hook`, `link_presets`, `faulthandler` and `enroll_fault_responder`.
- `Armature._verify_configuration_completed` (lines 220-221) only raises `NotImplementedError`. Each subclass supplies the real check.
- `App._verify_configuration_completed` (`src/quill/sansio/app.py:413`) guards on `_got_first_request` instead. This is the app's own version of the same rule.

**Why it exists**
- On enrollment, `Schematic.enroll` replays the schematic's recorded setup, including `deferred_functions`. It uses that to build the per-app state and to run `_combine_schematic_functions`.
- A route or handler added after that replay would be missing from apps that were already registered. It would appear only in apps registered later, so behavior would depend on registration order. Failing early avoids that.
- `enroll` also computes `first_bp_registration = not any(bp is self for bp in app.schematics.values())`. This is separate from the flag. It lets a schematic be registered several times, for example under different names or prefixes, without repeating one-time work.
- `CHANGES.rst` records that this was only a warning in 2.2.0 and became a hard error in 2.3.0.

Quill splits this into two parallel pieces. Each of the two classes that can own a static folder, `Quill` and `Schematic`, has its own static-serving view. Both views read the same config key for caching.

**Component model**
- `Armature` (`src/quill/sansio/skeleton.py`) is the shared base of `App` and `Schematic`. It holds the static settings: `fixed_dir`, `fixed_address_route`, the `owns_fixed_directory` property and `root_path`.
- `Schematic` is Quill's blueprint. It is defined in `src/quill/sansio/schematics.py` (setup, registration) and `src/quill/schematics.py` (runtime behavior). It is documented in `docs/schematics.rst`. The `Quill` app class is in `src/quill/app.py`.

**Static serving in each component**
- **App:** `Quill.__init__` (`src/quill/app.py:226-279`) registers the static rule when `owns_fixed_directory` is true. It first asserts that `bool(static_host) == host_matching`. It then calls `attach_link_regulation` for `<fixed_address_route>/<path:filename>`, using a weakref lambda that points at `dispatch_fixed_document`. The default rule is `/static/<filename>` with terminus `static`.
- **Schematic:** `Schematic.enroll` (`src/quill/sansio/schematics.py`, about L323-326) does the same at registration time. If `owns_fixed_directory` is true, it calls `state.attach_link_regulation(f"{self.fixed_address_route}/<path:filename>", view_func=self.dispatch_fixed_document, ...)`. The rule is therefore added to the app only when the schematic is enrolled, and it is subject to the schematic's `url_prefix`.
- **The two views:** `Quill.dispatch_fixed_document` (`src/quill/app.py:308-328`) and `Schematic.dispatch_fixed_document` (`src/quill/schematics.py:82-102`) match line for line. Each does the following:
  - It raises `RuntimeError("'fixed_dir' must be set to serve static_files.")` if no folder is set.
  - It gets a max age from `fetch_file_transfer_ttl()`.
  - It returns `dispatch_from_folder(fixed_dir, filename, max_age=max_age)`.

**How caching stays consistent**
- Both components define `fetch_file_transfer_ttl` (`src/quill/app.py:281-306` and `src/quill/schematics.py:55-80`).
- Both read `current_app.config['SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT']`, and both convert it the same way:
  - `None` stays `None`.
  - A `timedelta` becomes `int(total_seconds())`.
  - Any other value is returned as is.
- The value is read from `current_app`, not from the component itself. A schematic's static files therefore use the app-wide setting, and it needs an app context.
- Both views hand the result to the same helper, `dispatch_from_folder`, as `max_age`. That helper sits on top of `dispatch_document`, which handles etag and conditional responses. `CHANGES.rst` records the rename of `cache_timeout` to `max_age`.

**Caveats**
- `fetch_file_transfer_ttl` is duplicated in both classes rather than defined once in the base.
- `docs/schematics.rst` (L212-217) says a schematic's static folder cannot be reached without a `url_prefix`. The app's `/static` rule takes precedence, and static folders are not used as a fallback the way templates are.

The dual inheritance is a deliberate way to make an error be two kinds of exception at once. It does not separate validation failures from encoding issues. I also found no code that raises or catches `SurpriseCharsetFault`, so the design intent below is inferred from the class definition.

**The class**
- `SurpriseCharsetFault(AssertionError, UnicodeError)` is at `src/quill/diagnosticassistants.py:17-20`.
- Its docstring says it is "Raised in places where we want some better error reporting for unexpected unicode or binary data."
- The body has no methods, only the docstring.
- A search of the repository turns up only the definition (plus the `.micode` index). Nothing in `src/` or `tests/` raises or catches it.
- It is an unused, vestigial marker type. It appears to be a remnant of Flask's `UnexpectedUnicodeError`, renamed the way the rest of the codebase is. The `CHANGES.rst` gotcha about identifier substitutions describes that renaming.

**What each base class contributes**
- **`AssertionError`:** This is the marker used for debug-only diagnostics in this module.
  - `FormPayloadPathForwarding` (L50-78) is a plain `AssertionError`, and its message says it is raised only in debug mode.
  - `TroubleshootUploadsMissingKey` (L23-47) is `KeyError` plus `AssertionError`.
  - The setup-after-first-use guards also raise `AssertionError`.
  - The type tells a reader that a developer misused something. It is not a runtime data error.
- **`UnicodeError`:** This keeps the exception compatible with encoding and decoding handlers. Code that catches `UnicodeError` or `ValueError` around decoding would still catch it.

**What it says about the architecture**
- The module already follows one pattern. Each diagnostic class combines the original exception type with `AssertionError`. Existing handlers written for the original type keep working, and the extra debug-only detail is added on top. `TroubleshootUploadsMissingKey` does this with `KeyError`, and `SurpriseCharsetFault` does it with `UnicodeError`.
- The classes live in the separate `diagnosticassistants.py` module, and the debug decision is made by the caller. For example, `Request._read_form_payload` in `src/quill/envelope_types.py` (L197-210) only calls `append_encoding_fault_multimap` when `current_app.debug` is true. The diagnostics are a layer that does not run in production.
- The two concerns are not separated, and the class deliberately does the opposite. One exception object carries both a "the developer set this up wrongly" signal and an "encoding problem" signal.

There are two subdomain-routing tests in `tests/test_trialing.py`. Both run the same chain: configuration, then route registration, then request context creation. I've written it for `test_schematic_having_subhost` (L117-138) and noted where `test_hostprefix` (L302-318) differs.

**1. Configuration**
- `quill.Quill(__name__, subdomain_matching=True)` sets `App.subdomain_matching` (`src/quill/sansio/app.py:407`).
- `app.config["SERVER_NAME"] = "example.com:1234"` and `app.config["APPLICATION_ROOT"] = "/foo"` supply the host and path root.
- `app.test_caller()` (`src/quill/app.py:669`) builds a `QuillPatron` client (`src/quill/testing.py`) bound to the app. It doesn't read the config until a request is made.

**2. Route registration**
- `quill.Schematic("company", __name__, subdomain="xxx")` stores the subdomain on the schematic (`src/quill/sansio/schematics.py:203`).
- `@bp.route("/")` goes through `Armature.route`, which is wrapped by `preparationmethod`. The schematic records a deferred function.
- `app.enroll_plan(bp)` calls `Schematic.enroll`. That builds a registration state whose `subdomain` (L64-70) is filled into the rule options (L103). Each deferred function then calls `App.attach_link_regulation` (`src/quill/sansio/app.py:604-661`). This adds the `Rule` to `app.url_map` with the `xxx` subdomain and `/foo` prefix, and sets `view_functions["company.index"]`.
- `test_hostprefix` skips the schematic. It uses `@app.route("/", subdomain="<company_id>")` directly, which reaches `attach_link_regulation` through `Armature.route`.

**3. Request context creation**
- `app.test_call_scope("/", subdomain="xxx")` (`src/quill/app.py:1423-1477`) builds a `SurroundingsConstructor` (`src/quill/testing.py:49-86`).
  - With no `base_url`, it takes `http_host` from `SERVER_NAME` and prefixes the subdomain, giving `xxx.example.com:1234`.
  - It takes the scheme from `PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME` and appends `APPLICATION_ROOT`.
  - It passes the resulting environ to `app.query_environment(...)`, which returns the `InquiryScope`.
- Building the scope calls `app.build_link_adapter(request)` (`src/quill/ctx.py:323`, definition at `src/quill/app.py:425-466`).
  - Because `subdomain_matching` is true, it leaves the subdomain unforced and calls `url_map.bind_to_environ(environ, server_name=SERVER_NAME)`.
  - Without `subdomain_matching`, `build_link_adapter` forces the subdomain to the map's default.
- Matching the environ against the rule sets `request.url` to `http://xxx.example.com:1234/foo/`, which the test asserts. `request.schematic == bp.name` follows from the matched terminus `company.index`.

**4. Client dispatch**
- `client.get("/", subdomain="xxx")` builds a new `SurroundingsConstructor`. It runs the same environ construction through `QuillPatron.open`, and the app then handles the request. The view returns `quill.request.url`, so the body is the same URL.
- In `test_hostprefix`, the URL is built inside `with app.test_call_scope():`. `ctx.py:247` calls `build_link_adapter(None)`, which binds using `SERVER_NAME`, `APPLICATION_ROOT` and `PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME` because no request exists. `quill.build_link_to("view", company_id="xxx")` then runs against that adapter, and `client.get(url)` requests the built URL.

**Dependency order:** the app config must be set before any scope is created. Routes must be registered before `test_call_scope`. The context depends on both the config and the registered `url_map`.

Quill uses two mechanisms, depending on the kind of template function. Context processors are merged into the app's registry when a schematic is enrolled. Filters, tests and globals are written straight onto the shared Jinja environment. Both are in effect before any template renders.

**1. Recording on the schematic**
- `Armature.scope_enricher` (`src/quill/sansio/skeleton.py:542-555`) appends a context processor to `template_context_processors[None]`. The registry is created in `Armature.__init__` and is seeded with `_fallback_layout_scope_handler`, which supplies `g`, `request` and `session` (`src/quill/layouting.py:24-36`).
- Schematic-level processors are keyed by the schematic's name in the same dict.
- Setup methods are guarded by `preparationmethod`, so registration must happen before the schematic is enrolled.

**2. Merging into the app at enrollment**
- `Schematic.enroll` (`src/quill/sansio/schematics.py`) calls `_combine_schematic_functions(app, name)`.
- That function ends by calling `extend(self.template_context_processors, app.template_context_processors)` (L410). This copies the schematic's processors into the app's registry under the schematic's dotted name.
- Because the registry lives on the app, the schematic's processors are in place before any render.

**3. Filters, tests and globals go straight to the shared environment**
- `Schematic.program_layout_sieve`, `program_layout_probe` and `program_layout_universal`, and their `attach_...` variants (`schematics.py:443-551`), register a callback through `note_once_only` (L233). The callback runs only when `state.first_registration` is true.
- The callback sets `state.app.markup_engine_env.filters|tests|globals[name or f.__name__] = f` (L473, L511, L549).
- `program_scope_enricher` (`schematics.py:587-591`) appends to `app.template_context_processors[None]`, so its processors apply to every view's templates.
- On the app itself, `App` does the same directly (`src/quill/sansio/app.py:695, 738, 776`).
- `markup_engine_env` (`sansio/app.py:470`) is the app's single Jinja environment. It is created on first access through `build_layout_ecosystem` (`src/quill/app.py:385`) as an `Ecosystem` (`layouting.py:39-49`). Schematics and the app therefore share it.

**4. Availability at render time**
- `draw_layout` and `draw_layout_text` get the current app and use `app.markup_engine_env` to fetch or compile the template (`layouting.py:148-161`). They then call `_render` (L126-135). `flow_layout` and `flow_layout_text` do the same through `_stream`.
- `_render` first calls `app.refresh_layout_scope(context)` (`src/quill/app.py:506-532`).
  - It builds the lookup keys as `(None, *reversed(request.schematics))` when a request exists, otherwise just `(None,)`.
  - For each key it runs every registered processor and calls `context.update(...)`.
  - It then re-applies a copy of the original context, so values passed by the caller override processor values.
  - It runs processors through `guarantee_blocking`, which lets async processors work.
- `_render` then sends `before_render_template`, calls `template.render(context)`, and sends `template_rendered`.

**5. Template lookup across schematics**
- `Ecosystem` defaults its loader to `app.build_universal_layout_fetcher()`, which is a `RoutingTemplateFetcher` (`layouting.py:52-123`). It searches the app's template reader first, then each schematic's reader through `app.walk_plans()`.

**Details**
- Filters, tests and globals from a schematic are app-wide once it is enrolled, not scoped to the schematic. Only context processors get schematic scoping, through the `request.schematics` lookup.
- Registering the same schematic object again does not repeat the filter, test or global setup, because `note_once_only` checks `first_registration`.

When `os.fspath()` is called on a `MockLocation`, its `__fspath__` method returns `self.path`. That is the string given to the constructor, unchanged.

**The class**
- `MockLocation` is in `tests/test_aids.py:11-22`. Its docstring calls it a "Fake object to represent a ``PathLike object``" and says it stands in for a `pathlib.Path` in Python 3. It cites PEP 519.
- `__init__(self, path)` (L18-19) stores the argument as `self.path`.
- `__fspath__(self)` (L21-22) returns `self.path`.
- The `__fspath__` protocol requires a `str` or `bytes` return. The test always passes a `str`, so the result is a `str`.

**How it is used**
- `MockLocation` is used only at `tests/test_aids.py:71`, inside `TestDispatchDocument.test_fixed_document`.
- That test calls `app.dispatch_fixed_document(MockLocation("index.html"))`.
- Elsewhere in the framework, Werkzeug's `dispatch_document` and `dispatch_from_folder` call `os.fspath` on their path argument. So `dispatch_fixed_document` gets `"index.html"` back and serves that file.
- The test checks that the `max_age` behavior works with a `PathLike` argument too.
- It does not touch the filesystem or `pathlib`. Only the `__fspath__` protocol is exercised.

There is a related test at `tests/test_elementary.py:1448-1454`, `test_fixed_folder_with_pathlib_location`. It passes a real `pathlib.Path("static")` as `fixed_dir`, not `MockLocation`.

I've read the test and the code it calls, and I'm writing up the answer now.

**The test** is `test_pinpoint_program_throws` in `tests/test_terminal_tool.py:199-219`. It is parametrized over `(iname, aname)` pairs, which are the import name and the app name. Each pair is passed to `find_program(iname, aname)` inside `pytest.raises(MissingProgramFailure)`.

**The exception rule.** `find_program` (`src/quill/cli.py:241-264`) and `locate_program_by_text` (`cli.py:120-197`) turn every failure into `MissingProgramFailure`. Each parametrized case fails at a different step:

| Case | Where it fails | How it becomes `MissingProgramFailure` |
|---|---|---|
| `("notanapp.py", None)` | `__import__("notanapp.py")` raises `ImportError` | The traceback has one frame (`tb_next` is `None`), and `raise_if_not_found` defaults to `True`, so `find_program` raises "Could not import" (L254-255). |
| `("cliapp/app", None)` | Same, since a path is not a valid module name | Same branch. |
| `("cliapp.message.txt", None)` | Same, since there is no module `cliapp.message.txt` | Same branch. |
| `("cliapp.loadfailureprogram", None)` | The module is found, but an `ImportError` is raised inside it, so the traceback is deeper than one frame | L249-253 raises `MissingProgramFailure` with the formatted traceback. |
| `("cliapp.app", "notanapp")` | `getattr(module, name)` raises `AttributeError` | L169-172 wraps it as "Failed to find attribute". |
| `("cliapp.manufacturer", 'build_program2("foo")')` | Calling the factory with too few arguments raises `TypeError` | L179-187 wraps it only if `_invoked_with_bad_arguments(attr)` is true. |
| `("cliapp.manufacturer", "build_program(")` | `ast.parse` raises `SyntaxError` | L130-133 wraps it as "Failed to parse". |
| `("cliapp.manufacturer", "without_program")` | The result is not a `Quill` instance | L194-197 raises "A valid Quill application was not obtained". |

Every `raise ... from None` or `from e` replaces the lower-level exception, so the caller only ever sees `MissingProgramFailure`.

**Why each parameter matters.** `iname` chooses which stage fails: import, or the attribute and call stage. `aname` chooses which of the parse, lookup, call and type checks fails. A `None` `aname` goes to `locate_optimal_program` instead.

**Two boundaries that are deliberately not swallowed:**
- `raise_if_not_found=False` only suppresses a direct import failure, meaning the traceback has one frame. `test_pinpoint_program_mute_throw` (L222-228) checks this. `find_program("notanapp.py", None, raise_if_not_found=False)` returns `None`. A nested import failure in `cliapp.loadfailureprogram` still raises.
- A `TypeError` raised inside the factory is re-raised unchanged when `_invoked_with_bad_arguments` is false. That is a bug in user code, not a lookup failure. `test_locate_optimal_program` covers the equivalent case.

The "fails consistently" guarantee holds because `find_program` only catches `ImportError`, and `locate_program_by_text` converts its own failures itself. Anything else passes through unchanged.
